scope.scannerPackageSet: Package, lockfile, and source indicators for pre-execution review.
scope.currentCampaignContext: OX Security reported a DPRK-linked npm infostealer/RAT campaign involving terminal-logger-utils and dependent packages pretty-logger-utils, ts-logger-pack, and pinno-loggers. GitHub Advisory GHSA-m3gw-x6rc-fp3r reports csc154-internall-depend as npm malware with all versions affected. GitHub Advisory GHSA-vqg9-785x-8j39 reports @validate-sdk/v2 as npm malware with all versions affected. GitHub Advisory GHSA-g6v5-9xpp-6hpx reports google-cloud-secret-manager-config-poc as npm malware with all versions affected. GitHub Advisory GHSA-6vr2-5hpq-589c and supplychainattack.org report node-core-libs as npm malware requiring full-compromise handling if installed or run. GitHub Advisory GHSA-fr34-v6cp-fc49 and supplychainattack.org report normalize-plus as npm malware requiring full-compromise handling if installed or run. GitHub Advisory GHSA-m97m-v5gv-jm47 and supplychainattack.org report nabisco as npm malware requiring full-compromise handling if installed or run. GitHub Advisories GHSA-qp73-r9hh-6vq9 and GHSA-8j4q-hx83-pfq9 plus supplychainattack.org report ts-grok and signup-embedder as npm malware with affected versions >= 0 and no patched versions, requiring full-compromise handling if installed or run. Panther reports an April 2026 OtterCookie npm campaign using wrapper/payload packages with exact malicious versions and Vercel-hosted C2 infrastructure. JFrog reports Solana FakeFix and CMS Windows loader npm/PyPI packages targeting Solana keys, SSH keys, cloud credentials, source-control tokens, wallet files, and Windows persistence. Socket reports GlassWASM trojanized Open VSX extensions using suspicious WASM payloads, TinyGo/WebAssembly host code, Solana memo dead-drop retrieval, and child-process download/execute loaders. BleepingComputer reported Aikido findings on malicious JetBrains Marketplace plugins stealing AI API keys and exfiltrating to 39.107.60[.]51/api/software/key. DFIR Radar added June 25 implementation details for the same JetBrains plugin family: save/apply configuration persistence exfiltration, BaseUtil.request(), sk- key validation, static auth token F48D2AA7CF341F782C1D, and plaintext HTTP POST from JetBrains processes. Island and The Hacker News reported June 2026 Adblock for YouTube browser-extension risk: the live Chrome extension ID cmedhionkhpnakcndndgjdbohmhepckk, related removed extension IDs, api.adblock-for-youtube.com / get.adblock-for-youtube.com, Unistream infrastructure, and a dormant server-controlled trusted-create-element / MAIN-world scriptlet injection path. This checker detects those package/plugin/extension names and selected behavior indicators. OX Security reported the June 17, 2026 easy-day-js / Mastra npm supply-chain attack affecting 141 packages through a malicious dayjs dependency swap, postinstall setup.cjs execution, and crypto-stealer C2 indicators. Socket later published stage-2 easy-day-js / Mastra details, including protocal.cjs, nvmconf.service, NodePackages persistence, Hostwinds C2 hostnames, /update/49890878, wallet-extension inventory behavior, browser-history collection, and SHA-256 hashes. SafeDep reported a June 16, 2026 procwire / routecraft npm campaign in which five coordinated packages split a Windows-only preinstall dropper across procwire, routecraft, endpointmap, bytecraft, and staticlayer, reconstructing a catbox.moe payload URL, using Microsoft-Delivery-Optimization/10.0, curl.exe, bitsadmin, hidden process execution, and Mark-of-the-Web stripping. JFrog reported hijacked html-to-gutenberg@4.2.11 and fetch-page-assets@1.2.9 npm packages using VS Code folder-open tasks, a fake fa-solid-400.woff2 JavaScript payload, blockchain dead drops, socket.io backdoor behavior, and Python infostealer staging; Nextron reported related Go-package reuse of the same fake-font payload hashes as OSINT follow-up. JFrog's June 25, 2026 Shai-Hulud/Hades analysis adds affected @immobiliarelabs/backstage-plugin-gitlab and ldap-auth package versions plus SEED_PAT/Seeder operator-seeding markers to the Leo/RStreams Miasma/Hades npm lane. Aikido also warned that the ImmobiliareLabs Backstage LDAP auth and GitLab plugins are credential-stealing worm targets; hits on those auth/backend packages should trigger clean-device rotation of GitHub, npm, LDAP, Backstage, CI, and cloud credentials after containment. SafeDep's June 25 LeoPlatform follow-up confirms 20 compromised LeoPlatform npm package versions and adds repository poisoning details around orphan snapshot-* branches, fake Dependabot Updates workflows, _index.js execution, OIDC_PACKAGES, WORKFLOW_ID, REPO_ID_SUFFIX, and NPM_TOKEN publication surfaces. JFrog's June 18, 2026 npm v12 trust-model analysis reinforces this pre-execution lane: allowScripts, --allow-git, and --allow-remote move npm from implicit execution/retrieval to explicit approvals, but approvals should be version-pinned, temporary, and re-evaluated because attackers can target already-approved packages or move logic to runtime/import-time paths. Microsoft published AutoJack research on a local AI-agent/browser-to-localhost control-plane RCE pattern in AutoGen Studio, fixed in GitHub main at commit b047730. The Hacker News reported that autogenstudio pre-release builds 0.4.3.dev1 and 0.4.3.dev2 contained the vulnerable MCP WebSocket handler, while the stable PyPI build 0.4.2.2 did not include that route. This checker flags those pre-release references and selected AutoJack local MCP control-plane indicators for review. August 4, 2026 keyv/cacheable (ChainDrop / Shai-Hulud "Here We Go Again") wave: exact-version indicators for the initial full-worm carriers keyv@6.0.0, flat-cache@6.1.24, file-entry-cache@11.1.6, cacheable-request@13.0.20, cacheable@2.5.1, @cacheable/memory@2.2.1, cache-manager@7.2.10, @cacheable/node-cache@3.1.2, @cacheable/utils@2.5.1, @cacheable/net@2.1.1, and ecto@5.0.1, credited to Snyk, StepSecurity, Aikido, Wiz, and JFrog reporting. This keyv/cacheable wave is cross-platform npm ecosystem risk (any OS/lane), not a Linux-only host issue; credits Snyk, StepSecurity, Aikido, Wiz, and JFrog.
